final_answer: The computational security of AES-256 against brute-force attacks is considered strong, but there are attacks that require significant computational resources. For example, an attack against AES-256 that uses only two related keys and operates on a 9-round version requires 2^239 operations, while an attack on a 10-round version requires 2^245 operations. These attacks are not practical on current or foreseeable hardware. [Citation: Advanced Encryption Standard documents retrieved from the knowledge base]
